takeaway: SUFE: overweight boys around puberty (10-15 years). Perthes is younger (4-10), hip dysplasia is newborn, and septic arthritis or NOF fracture are rare at this age.

question.text: An obese 15-year-old boy presents with pain in the hip. He walks with an antalgic gait with some shortening of the affected limb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
question.say: An obese fifteen-year-old boy presents with pain in the hip. He walks with an antalgic gait with some shortening of the affected limb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

lines.text: An obese fifteen-year-old boy limps with a painful hip.
This classic picture fits overweight boys around puberty, ten to fifteen years.
Like ice cream sliding off its cone, the epiphysis slips off the femoral neck.
lines.say: (laugh) Like ice cream sliding off its cone, the epiphysis slips off the femoral neck.

lines.text: Perthes disease also favours boys, but younger ones, four to ten years.
Hip dysplasia shows in the newborn or the first few years.
Septic arthritis and hip fracture are very rare at fifteen, and usually stop weight bearing.
So the diagnosis is slipped upper femoral epiphysis.
